title: Library document summaries
validatorNotApplicable: each file is a `library-summary/v1` record for ONE library entry (`library-summaries/<doc-id>.json`: `doc_id`, `source_sha256`, `brief`, `extended`, `sections`, `tokens`, `provenance`), not a graph node. `scripts/summarize-library.py --check` regenerates the scan index from them and fails when `library/INDEX.md` is stale; a record whose `doc_id` or `source_sha256` no longer matches its entry's `structure.json` is rebuilt on the next `--apply`, except one whose `provenance.kind` is `agent`, which is never overwritten.
summary: One document-level summary per library entry: a brief of at most 200 characters (the line `library/INDEX.md` carries) and an extended summary of about 500 tokens, read to decide whether a document is worth opening.

avatar.reads: a page of short lines: a summary of a longer document

rationale: Owner decision 2026-11-24 (card answer "C1 migrate", PR #9396): qou's library must pass the platform's library gate (`check:l1-complete`), whose closed set of entry children has no document-level summary. These records lived inside each entry as `library/<doc-id>/summary.json` and were reported as strays in 803 entries. The platform's own `summaries.json` is a different object (one agent narrative per PROSE BLOCK, `folio-block-summaries/v1`), so renaming into it would have conflated the two. Kept beside the library instead, one file per entry, so the three-tier walk of AGENTS.md corpus-grep path 5 (INDEX.md, then the summary, then sections/) is unchanged in everything but this one path. `derived`: the extractive records are regenerated by `scripts/summarize-library.py`; the agent-written ones (`provenance.kind: agent`) are preserved by it.
